gen-press-start-2p-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Pixel-arcade nostalgia, right up front. Press Start 2P keeps its strokes nearly uniform and its letters spaced far apart, while Noto Sans Osmanya answers with wide-turning s shapes and a lowercase that towers over its capitals.
gen-tourney-gf-hind-vadodara: Chunky, stretched-out, built for the scoreboard. Tourney spreads its blocky letters wide at one width, and Hind Vadodara settles beneath with rounded glyphs whose gaps stay generous and a thickness that never wavers.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curves loose and its lowercase full. Tourney is best at stretched, bulky, single-width punch, whereas the body font does its finest work in those tall, open c, s and z forms.
gen-tourney-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hiero: Blunt, marker-tipped and loud. Tourney is best at that stretched, bulky shout, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs does its finest work in outward-pointing tips and a lowercase rising nearly to cap height.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-readex-pro: Bouncy, bold letters with their mouths held open. Readex Pro takes over below with broad terminal gaps and a weight that never shifts from word to word, so a long passage would move along steadily.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-quicksand: Tight, tall and sure of itself. Oswald packs its rows into dense, confident blocks, while Quicksand is best at rounded, bulb-like lowercase drawn in a uniform line, soft against the heading's strength.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-akatab: Narrow, strong and tightly knit. Akatab follows with round letters that look cupped rather than clenched, so if Oswald were made small, that heading density would lose its punch beside it.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-nko: Dense, confident and tightly packed. Oswald sets the tone up top, and Noto Sans NKo follows with c openings you can see through, so a longer passage would feel modern and easy to move through.
